claim: For unlabeled ecological abundance profiles with strictly positive integer species counts and fixed total census size \(N\), Shannon diversity \(H_S=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i\) and Brillouin diversity \(H_B=N^{-1}[\log(N!)-\sum_i\log(n_i!)]\) induce exactly the same weak ordering for every \(N\le6\). At \(N=7\), weak-order agreement first fails only because Brillouin ties \((1,1,1,4)\) with \((2,2,3)\) while Shannon ranks the former higher. No strict reversal occurs through \(N=7\). At \(N=8\), opposite strict rankings appear for the first time, in exactly two unordered profile pairs up to species permutation: \((1,1,1,5)\) versus \((2,2,4)\), and \((1,1,6)\) versus \((4,4)\). In both pairs Shannon ranks the first profile as more diverse, while Brillouin ranks the second as more diverse. At fixed \(N\), Shannon ordering is the reverse ordering of \(Q=\prod_i n_i^{n_i}\), while Brillouin ordering is the reverse ordering of \(F=\prod_i n_i!\); the complete cutoff follows by exact enumeration of all integer partitions through \(N=8\).
integrity: At fixed census total the two rankings reduce exactly to integer invariants: Q=product n_i^{n_i} for Shannon and F=product n_i! for Brillouin. All integer partitions through total eight are generated exhaustively and partition counts are independently cross-checked.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns unlabeled strictly positive integer abundance profiles, exact raw Shannon and Brillouin diversity, and common finite census total. It does not address normalized evenness variants, sampling uncertainty, or arbitrary real-valued abundance vectors.
title: Eight individuals are the sharp Shannon–Brillouin strict-ranking boundary
